findings.current: What made it worse was that they had occurred in the capitals and major cities of countries everyone knew by name.
findings.defect: The draft changes “capitals or major cities” to “capitals and major cities” and incorrectly makes the countries, rather than the cities, the familiar names.
findings.rationale: The source uses 혹은, meaning “or,” and describes the attack sites themselves as widely recognizable.
findings.replacement: What made it worse was that the attacks had occurred in capitals or major cities whose names were known around the world.
findings.source: 더군다나 사건의 발생지는 이름만 들어도 아는 각 나라의 수도, 혹은 대도시들.

findings.current: “We obtained this footage when the first Monster Wave occurred in Paris. This is a video recorded by Odin Guild.”
findings.defect: The second sentence is an unsupported addition that changes Odin Guild from the party that obtained the footage to the party that recorded it.
findings.rationale: 입수한 means “obtained” or “acquired”; the source never says Odin Guild recorded the video.
findings.replacement: “This is footage Odin Guild obtained when the first Monster Wave occurred in Paris.”
findings.source: “파리에서의 첫 몬스터 웨이브 발생 당시, 저희 오딘 길드가 입수한 영상입니다.”

findings.current: > **Odin Guild Master Michael Silbert: “This was a meticulously planned terrorist attack, not a Monster Wave.”**
findings.defect: The draft denies that the event was a Monster Wave, although the source characterizes it as planned terrorism before or beyond its classification as a Monster Wave.
findings.rationale: 몬스터 웨이브 이전에 does not negate the Monster Wave; it establishes terrorism as the underlying nature or cause of the event.
findings.replacement: > **Odin Guild Master Michael Silbert: “Before this was a Monster Wave, it was a meticulously planned terrorist attack.”**
findings.source: [오딘 길드장 미카엘 실베르트, “이것은 몬스터 웨이브 이전에, 치밀하게 계획된 테러다.”]

findings.current:
A mysterious vigilante whose face, name, and even gender were unknown.

The leaders of terrorist and rebel groups had been beheaded by that vigilante, and the two factions, suddenly deprived of their leadership, had suffered enormous losses after fierce internal struggles before being forced to raise the white flag.
findings.defect: The draft turns the explicitly plural vigilantes into a single individual, changing the number and subject responsible for the killings.
findings.rationale: The source subsequently refers to the vigilantes as 그들, “they,” establishing that the mysterious vigilante force comprises multiple people.
findings.replacement:
A mysterious group of vigilantes whose faces, names, and even genders were unknown.

They had beheaded the leaders of the terrorist and rebel groups, and the two factions, suddenly deprived of their leadership, suffered enormous losses in the fierce internal struggles that followed and were forced to raise the white flag.
findings.source:
얼굴과 이름, 심지어는 성별조차 알려지지 않은 의문의 자경단.

그들에 의해 테러리스트와 반군 집단의 수뇌부는 목이 날아갔고, 한순간에 지도층을 잃은 두 세력은 치열한 내부다툼 끝에 엄청난 피해를 입고 백기를 내걸어야 했다.

findings.current: But ten countries, including the United States, are implicated in this attack.
findings.defect: “Implicated” suggests that the ten countries were culpable in the terrorism rather than countries caught up in or affected by it.
findings.rationale: The surrounding discussion identifies these as 피해국, affected countries, and argues that striking ten countries would be implausible for the weakened groups.
findings.replacement: But this terrorist attack involved ten countries, including the United States.
findings.source: 그런데 이번 테러에 연루된 나라만 미국 포함 10개국임.

findings.current:
>> That doesn’t mean what he did was right.

>> Fine, you’re right. But let’s be precise. Everyone justified it back then. Now that one unbelievably insane bastard has appeared, you’re all switching sides at the speed of light.

>> Domestic and overseas, everyone praised the vigilante back then. “Whoever you are, great job. Let’s not bother finding out.” That was the atmosphere. Now it’s completely reversed.
findings.defect: The draft omits two rebuttals, a separate accusation and response about Jin Taekyung’s character, and the entire explanation that his vigilantism occurred just before the Mana Cultivation Method was released. It consequently conflates comments from three separate threads and removes the central causal argument.
findings.rationale: The omitted exchange supplies the opposing moral argument, defends Jin’s established demeanor, and explains the timing and intended preventive rationale behind the killings.
findings.replacement:
>> That doesn’t mean what he did was right.

>> So it was fine then but not now? You’re fucking crazy, lol.

>> The situation has changed. Seriously, how many people are dead now? Nationalist hype and personal fandom are all well and good, but look at how serious the situation has become because of what Jin Taekyung did.

> I knew that bastard Jin Taekyung would cause trouble. I hated watching him get full of himself from the moment people started hyping him up as a young hero and the next Cheon Taemin.

>> That’s complete bullshit. When was he ever full of himself? Even when the media was hyping him nonstop, hyung still walked around in a tracksuit.

> Putting it neutrally, I personally just think it’s unfortunate. Do you really think Jin Taekyung did that because he was some bloodthirsty killer?

>> Then why did he do it?

>> Look at the timing. It was right before the Mana Cultivation Method was released. Seriously, do you think there are only one or two Awakened among the Middle Eastern terrorists and African rebel groups? Who was supposed to deal with them if they learned the Mana Cultivation Method and started committing every kind of crime, including terrorism?

>> That still doesn’t justify murder.

>> Fine, you’re right. But let’s be precise. Everyone justified it back then. Now that one unbelievably insane bastard has appeared, you’re all switching sides at the speed of light.

>> At the time, people both at home and abroad were universally praising the vigilantes. “Whoever you are, great job. Let’s not bother finding out who they are.” That was the atmosphere, and now it has completely reversed.

findings.current: People watching the video swallowed unconsciously.
findings.defect: The literal wording is unnatural and omits that they involuntarily caught or held their breath.
findings.rationale: 숨을 삼켰다 describes an involuntary interruption of breathing from shock, not ordinary swallowing.
findings.replacement: The people watching the video caught their breath without realizing it.
findings.source: 영상을 지켜보던 사람들은 자신도 모르게 숨을 삼켰다.

findings.rationale: The source ends with two literal semicolons; `; ;` is an accidental Markdown/HTML artifact.

findings.current: A silver tray in one hand, his gaze fixed on the screen of the smartphone in his other.
findings.defect: The draft renders the complete source sentence as a dangling sentence fragment.
findings.rationale: The source has a complete finite statement describing where the Skeleton King’s gaze was fixed.
findings.replacement: Holding a silver tray in one hand, he kept his gaze fixed on the smartphone in the other.
findings.source: 은빛 쟁반을 손에 든 그의 시선은 다른 한 손에 들린 스마트폰의 화면에 고정되어 있었다.

summary: The draft contains several factual reversals and omissions, including altered attack locations, false footage provenance, denial that the terrorist incidents were Monster Waves, a singularized vigilante group, victim countries framed as implicated parties, and a substantially truncated online debate.
